purpose: Audit standalone app deployment candidates without moving files, renaming folders, rewriting registries, changing livePath values, or deploying anything from this batch.

summary.candidateSource: data/site-registry.json records with type nextjs-app / needsStandaloneDeploy plus package.json inspection.
summary.recommendedStrategy: Treat the portfolio as the discovery/index layer. Promote high-value apps to dedicated repositories or dedicated Vercel projects only after build verification and business-priority review.
summary.notes: Batch 17 does not deploy, move, rename, or normalize any folders. It creates planning metadata only.

candidates.title: Financing Widget
candidates.frameworkGuess: Next.js App Router or Pages Router candidate
frameworkEvidence: scripts include next dev, next build, next start
candidates.packageManager: unknown; likely npm unless lockfile inspection proves otherwise
candidates.outputType: server-rendered/static-capable Next.js app; requires build inspection before static-export assumptions
candidates.likelyVercelStrategy: Create a dedicated Vercel project with root directory set to financing-widget. Framework preset: Next.js. Build command: npm run build. Output directory: Vercel default.
candidates.separateRepoRecommendation: Promote to a dedicated financing-widget or embedded-finance-widget repo if it becomes a real lead-capture product.
candidates.recommendedUse: embedded-finance lead magnet / B2B partner widget
candidates.targetAudience: B2B partners, referral partners, business owners seeking financing, embedded finance users
candidates.recommendedNextAction: Run a local or Vercel preview build audit, confirm routes and forms, then decide whether to split into a dedicated repo/project.
risks: React 19 and Next 15 dependency stack may require modern Vercel defaults.
Widget positioning suggests embed behavior should be tested separately from standalone site deployment.
Lead capture and compliance copy should be reviewed before public promotion.
candidates.notes: Highest-priority standalone candidate because it maps directly to financing lead capture and partner enablement.

candidates.title: Moonshine Affiliate Hub
frameworkEvidence: scripts include next dev, next build, next start, next lint, and typecheck
candidates.packageManager: unknown; likely npm unless lockfile inspection proves otherwise
candidates.outputType: Next.js application; likely deployable as a dedicated Vercel project after build/typecheck review
candidates.likelyVercelStrategy: Create a dedicated Vercel project with root directory set to moonshine-affiliate-hub. Framework preset: Next.js. Build command: npm run build. Output directory: Vercel default.
candidates.separateRepoRecommendation: Promote to a dedicated Moonshine affiliate/partner enablement app repo if it becomes the operational hub for partners.
candidates.recommendedUse: affiliate partner enablement hub / internal partner OS candidate
candidates.targetAudience: Moonshine Capital affiliates, referral partners, partner managers, broker-recruitment workflows
candidates.recommendedNextAction: Run typecheck/build, inspect routes and onboarding flows, and compare against the static partner enablement assets before deciding on a standalone deployment.
risks: May overlap with existing static partner enablement assets and should not fragment the partner experience unless it becomes the canonical app.
React 19 / Next 15 stack should be build-tested before promotion.
Affiliate claims, commission language, and partner CTAs need copy/compliance review.
candidates.notes: Strategically valuable, but should be positioned carefully against existing partner enablement and affiliate recruitment flows.

candidates.title: Moonshine Editorial Bento
frameworkEvidence: scripts include next dev, next build, next start, and next lint
candidates.packageManager: unknown; likely npm unless lockfile inspection proves otherwise
candidates.outputType: Next.js application; possibly content/editorial microsite candidate
candidates.likelyVercelStrategy: Create a dedicated Vercel project with root directory set to Moonshine Editorial Bento. Framework preset: Next.js. Build command: npm run build. Output directory: Vercel default.
candidates.separateRepoRecommendation: Keep in portfolio until its editorial/content-ops role is clearer. Consider moving only if it becomes a canonical Moonshine content product.
candidates.targetAudience: Internal content operators, Moonshine editorial/content planning workflows

Business purpose is less direct than the financing and affiliate hub candidates.
Folder name contains spaces; keep as-is until slug normalization planning.
candidates.notes: Useful as a design/content prototype, but not the first standalone deployment candidate.

sourcePackageCandidates.description: The static extraction registry includes many Next.js ZIP packages that were classified as nextjs-app-needs-standalone-deploy but also had static HTML alternatives extracted. These are source-package candidates, not primary standalone app folders yet.
sourcePackageCandidates.recommendedHandling: Keep these ZIP/source packages preserved. Promote only after a specific asset proves more valuable than its extracted static version.

recommendedNextBatchFollowups: Run a build-readiness audit for financing-widget first.
Decide whether moonshine-affiliate-hub should become the canonical partner app or remain a prototype.
Fold reusable editorial ideas from Moonshine Editorial Bento into content hub strategy unless a standalone use case emerges.
